title: An inclusion disagreement must be resolved in public with the reasoning on record, not just the outcome
content:
A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3.1 handles the case where the GovOps meeting cannot reach consensus on including an item. The disagreement "must be raised in the govops channel in Slack so that the Spell Teams, Core GovOps, the Core Facilitator, and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead have visibility into the disagreement and the reasoning behind it," and the Core Facilitator "must hear all positions and make the final decision," which "is binding for the Executive Vote in question."

The provision then closes the obvious workaround: "A disagreement over whether to include an item must not... be resolved in a way that excludes the Core Facilitator or that settles the matter privately and reports only the outcome. The positions of each party, and the reasoning through which the disagreement is resolved, must be visible in the govops channel."

Banning private-resolution-plus-clean-report is the load-bearing part. A process that only requires outcomes to be visible is trivially satisfied by pre-negotiating in a side channel and announcing consensus — and the record then shows unanimity where there was a dispute. Requiring the *positions and reasoning* makes disagreement itself an artifact.

Even the necessary exception preserves this. Where security or confidentiality forces a private discussion, "the parties to that discussion must afterwards provide a substantive accounting in the govops channel... setting out the positions of each party and how the settled position was reached." Confidentiality can move the venue and delay the record; it cannot erase it.

The reason this matters beyond etiquette is that the reasoning is the only durable input for later review. A dissent that was recorded can be revisited if the decision turns out badly; a dissent that was smoothed over before it reached the channel leaves nothing to learn from.
description: A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3.1 forbids settling privately and reporting only the result; even a security-driven private discussion owes a substantive after-the-fact accounting of each party's position.
